dedupe_keys.name: faa advisory circular 150 5200 31c airport emergency plan

description: Advisory Circular 150/5200-31C gives airport operators guidance on developing and implementing an Airport Emergency Plan that covers the safety of and emergency services for the airport population and the surrounding community. It is issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration; the consolidated version with Change 1 is dated 1 May 2010 and was mandatory for airports certificated under 14 CFR Part 139 by 31 December 2010, while other airports are encouraged to use it alongside the national incident management directives. The 286-page document sets the format of a plan (basic plan, functional sections such as command and control, communications, alert notification, protective actions, law enforcement, firefighting, health and medical, resource management and airport operations, and hazard-specific sections), a systematic hazard identification with a hazards vulnerability analysis worksheet, estimated casualty tables, plan review and exercise evaluation checklists, definitions and guidance on mutual aid agreements with local, state and federal agencies. Coverage: US airports. Access: free PDF from the FAA document library. Licence and cost: US Government work, free. Caveats: guidance dating from 2010, with no data on actual plans or incidents, and details vary by airport. It helps define emergency response roles, resources and scenarios for airport disruption models. It relates to the FAA ASIAS safety data and NASR aeronautical data in the catalogue.
